programme.title: Imagine...
programme.sub-title: Rose Wylie: This Rose is Blooming
programme.desc: Very few people would have recognised the name Rose Wylie until this remarkable artist was in her mid 70s. Youthful, playful and unpredictable at the age of 83, she is an artist in her prime, her exuberant large-scale canvasses exhibited worldwide.

programme.title: Nature and Us: A History through Art
programme.desc: James explores how Piet Mondrian gradually leaves nature behind, tidying up the messy reality of nature into abstract lines. Meet artist Yang Yongliang whose sprawling digital landscapes ask questions about the drive for rapid urbanisation.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Joyce Grenfell, Robin Ray and Derek Hart. The guest musician is soprano Isobel Baillie.

programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programme.desc: From the bone-dry deserts of the Atacama, where penguins weave their way through a minefield of snapping sea lions, to the lush cloud forests of the Andes, where Andean bears scale 30-metre trees in search of elusive fruits, South America is full of the unusual and ingenious.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke tells the story of Ancient Egyptian art and how it reflected the civilisation's religion, through thirty extraordinary masterpieces.

programme.desc: Focuses on the development of the fortress, featuring examples in Warwick, Edinburgh and Conwy. At Hadrian's Wall Fred marvels at the design of Roman toilets, and he's joined by a band of knights in armour to test a castle's defences.

programme.title: Sorry!
programme.desc: Timothy's mother is mortified when he decides to move in with two attractive girls.

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: The story of Edward I, known to many as the villainous king in the Hollywood film `Braveheart', who tried to force English rule on Scotland and Wales, but found the resultant slaughter only served to inspire bold declarations of independence. When the king was eventually forced to listen to the parliament of his own people, England would also learn what it meant to be a nation.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: A Storyville documentary, set against the backdrop of conflict in Sudan, that follows five Khartoum residents as they search for freedom amid revolution and war.

programme.title: The Girl Who Talked to Dolphins
programme.desc: Documentary telling the story of the most extraordinary experiment in the history of animal science. In the 1960s a powerful and charismatic scientist flooded a house. He then invited a young woman to live there full-time with a dolphin.

programme.title: The Unseen Alistair Cooke
programme.desc: A revealing portrait of one of the most celebrated broadcasters of the 20th century, Alisdair Cooke, whose Radio 4 programme `Letter from America' spanned 58 years. Seen for the first time are extraordinary 8mm home movies shot by Cooke from 1933 onwards, charting his discovery of America, his passions and his friendships, including his close friendship with Charlie Chaplin.

programme.desc: This film celebrates the grandeur of Hampton Court Palace and visits Cragside, one of the first homes to have electric lighting. Fred Dibnah also examines restoration work on a 15th century manor house.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks: Coast to Coast
programme.desc: Richmond is the starting point for the longest section of Julia's adventure, a town which Wainwright enjoyed. Miles of flat walking await as Julia sets off across the broad vale between the Dales and her last National Park. The reward is the rugged escarpment of the North York Moors, offering the broadest views and the finest weather of the journey.

programme.title: My Garden of a Thousand Bees
programme.desc: Wildlife film-maker Martin Dohrn is bee obsessed. He has found over 60 species in his Bristol garden, from giant bumblebees to scissor bees the size of a mosquito, which he films with mind-blowing results. Dohrn can identify individual insects and forms a remarkable relationship with one leaf-cutter bee he follows through its entire life.

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: An introduction to John Stubbs's 18th-century masterpiece The Grosvenor Hunt. Written and narrated by John Jacob.

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: Jim encounters ever larger cosmic structures to reveal the latest breakthroughs in understanding of the universe. For example, there's the heliosphere, a vast cloud of solar plasma that surrounds and protects the solar system. Its unique physics help people understand why life is possible. Larger still, Jim comes face to face with our galactic home the Milky Way, a monstrous structure sculpted by the gravitational forces of dark matter.

programme.title: This Life
programme.desc: Egg takes on a medical negligence case and becomes emotionally involved with a client who has cancer. Meanwhile, Warren discovers the truth about Delilah, and Miles chooses a bad person in whom to confide about his love life.

programme.title: This Life
programme.desc: Delilah outstays her welcome, Anna resorts to devious means to get her way, and Warren loses his cool over a muesli yoghurt.

programme.title: Vasa: The Ghost Ship
programme.desc: The Vasa, one of the most majestic galleons ever put to sea, sank 18 minutes after leaving Stockholm harbour on her maiden voyage in 1628. Following the work of archaeologists, divers and historians as they investigate the sinking.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks: Coast to Coast
programme.desc: Julia sets out on the final stage. Robin Hood's Bay is the goal, but first she must complete the North York Moors and walk through Eskdale, before getting a first glimpse of the North Sea. The woods of Littlebeck and the clifftop finale provide an opportunity to reflect on a great adventure.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Using 70 years of BBC history archive film, Professor Alice Roberts uncovers how the iconic ancient monument of Stonehenge has been interpreted, argued over and debated by some of Britain's leading historians and archaeologists. She reveals how new discoveries would discredit old theories, how astronomers and geologists became involved in the story and why, even after centuries of study, there's still no definitive answer to the mystery of Stonehenge.

programme.title: Julian Barnes: Beyond the Page
programme.desc: Julian Barnes: How a 'very unconfident man' went on to be feted as one of the best of British novelists of the 1980s. Scaling the heights of literary greatness with works such as Flaubert's Parrot and The Sense of an Ending, he's now penned his final novel. The award-winning writer talks to the BBC's culture editor, Katie Razzall about his career, his thoughts on death and saying farewell to his novels and readers.

programme.title: The Sense of an Ending
programme.desc: A middle-aged business owner who lives a quiet life in London reunites with his first love after his mother unexpectedly receives a letter from his ex-girlfriend from school which forces him to confront the past.

programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks to...
programme.desc: Julian Barnes won the 2011 Man Booker Prize for `The Sense of an Ending' and his latest novel, `Levels of Life' is a memoir of bereavement following the loss of his wife to cancer. Here he talks to Mark Lawson about love, death, memory and grief.

programme.title: Brethyn & Fflwff

programme.title: Sion Y Chef

programme.title: Octonots
programme.desc: When a population of crawfish is struck by illness, the Octonauts race to find a cure.

programme.title: Byd Tad-cu
programme.desc: 'Pam bod y tymhorau'n newid?' yw cwestiwn Nanw heddiw, ac mae gan Dad-cu ateb dwl a doniol. Grandpa spins a tale about 4 rhubarb-loving monsters and the girl who teaches them a lesson!

programme.title: Blociau Rhif
programme.desc: Hwyl a sbri i blant ifanc gyda'r blociau rhif. Fun and games for young children's learning involving number blocks.

programme.title: Crawc a'i Ffrindiau
programme.desc: Mae Pigog, Gwich, Dan a Crawc yn mynd lan yr afon i chwilio am y Graig Canu ddirgel. Pigog, Gwich, Dan and Crawc go on a boat journey upriver to find the mysterious Song Stone.

programme.title: Bendibwmbwls
programme.desc: Heddiw mae Ben Dant yn ymuno a disgyblion Ysgol Y Graig, Merthyr Tudful, i greu trysor penigamp. Ben Dant joins the pupils of Ysgol Y Graig, Merthyr, to create a superb treasure.

programme.title: Twm Twrch
programme.desc: Mae Llyfryn wedi rhwygo un o'i dudalennau wrth chwarae cuddio ac wedi dechrau byhafio'n rhyfedd a chreu swynion od. A Booklet tears one of its pages while playing hide and seek and has begins to bark strangely and create odd spells.

programme.title: Ne-wff-ion
programme.desc: Dysgwn am fforio a sut i wneud pesto suran gydag Ewen, ac mae Louie yn Llanelli yn coginio pizza gyda Chegin y Bobo. A focus on food. We learn about foraging and how to make sorrel pesto.

programme.title: Sam Tân
programme.desc: Mae Jams yn gofyn a gofyn i Malcolm os allith e fod yn ddirprwy iddo, ac mae Jams yn datrys Pwy wnaeth ddwyn y brechdanau? James keeps asking Malcolm whether he can be his deputy.

programme.title: Ahoi!
programme.desc: Mae Ben Dant a Cadi wedi glanio ar Ynys Bendibelliawn, ond mae Capten Cnec wedi cipio'r ynys! Can the little pirates from Ysgol Cwmbran help Ben Dant and Cadi capture their island back?

programme.title: Twt
programme.desc: Toot's new periscope lets him see underwater like Sasha the Submarine, but can Sasha find something exciting for Toot to look at?

programme.title: Ein Byd Bach Ni
programme.desc: Ein thema ni y tro hyn yw, Oer. Byddwn yn dysgu mwy am eira a sut mae'n ffurfio, a ble yn y byd sy'n cael lot fawr o eira. We'll learn more about snow and how and where it's formed.

programme.title: Awyr Iach
programme.desc: Mae Meleri a'r criw yn chwilio am micro-blastigau ar draeth Amroth ac ma criw o ddisgyblion Ysgol Penboyr wrthi'n garddio. Huw joins Nanw and Gwenno on their favourite Menai Strait walk.

programme.title: Olobobs
programme.desc: Trying to return a mysterious pot to its owner, the Olobobs climb a rainbow and draw in the sky with magic paint.
